title: Wanna bet?
coreMove: Make a belief name its price before treating its confidence as real.
sourcePressure: The chapter turns confident claims into priced beliefs so the gap between tone and real conviction becomes visible.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: The writer must keep bet language as calibration, not social pressure; the stake reveals confidence instead of humiliating the other person.

sourceAnchors.name: Wanna bet?
sourceAnchors.detail: The source names the question as a calibration move that exposes the difference between confident speech and real willingness to stake.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: The small question changes the air because the claim has to become a price, not just a posture.

sourceAnchors.name: priced belief
sourceAnchors.detail: The source treats bet language as a way to make belief measurable through confidence levels, stakes, or probabilities.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Once the belief has a price, tone stops doing the work that evidence should do.

sourceAnchors.name: confident claim meeting a stake
sourceAnchors.detail: The source highlights how strong declarations often soften once the speaker must say what they would actually risk on them.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: A claim that sounded certain a minute ago may become a range the moment it has to carry a stake.

hook: Put your money where your mouth is
counterintuition: The loudest person should be challenged publicly
tryThisNow: Turn every claim into a wager

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples, drawn from: timestamp+name+action, dialogue first line, sensory detail first, second-person direct address, retrospective, question-as-hook, environmental detail before any human
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: C8 catches Cartesian repetition of phrases but not the deeper template of 'timestamp + named protagonist + prop + decision' that makes 6 examples feel like 1 example with name swaps

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one paragraph 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm - a question to the reader, a research aside, a direct second-person passage, or a brief historical reference
rhythmVariety.forbiddenRhythm: every paragraph following the pattern 'concrete anchor sentence -> abstract rule sentence -> elaboration sentence'

exampleSpecs.stakes: brewing too much ties up tanks; brewing too little loses summer accounts
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Sarah asks the brewer to turn "we will sell out" into a confidence percentage and batch size he would defend before ordering hops.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: The taproom smells like citrus hops while the empty keg labels wait in a stack.

exampleSpecs.stakes: a photographer is overconfident about weather risk and underprices a refund clause
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: What would Tomás actually stake on "it never rains here in June"? He checks ten years of venue dates and changes the contract language from certainty to odds.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: What would Tomás actually stake on the sentence he keeps saying to nervous couples?

exampleSpecs.domain: startup runway estimate before a seed extension
exampleSpecs.stakes: overstated confidence could push the company into a payroll cliff
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: At the board packet review, Anya replaces "we are fine through November" with confidence bands tied to three customer-payment dates.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: At 7:42 a.m., Anya deletes the word fine from the runway slide.

exampleSpecs.stakes: too many slots wastes staff time; too few leaves vulnerable patients waiting
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Michael asks each planner to write the odds behind their attendance estimate before the signup portal opens, then compares the spread rather than the volume of their voices.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: The waiting room chairs are stacked against the wall while the appointment grid glows on the monitor.

exampleSpecs.stakes: a boastful target changes ad spend and volunteer shifts
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Olivia sees that the pledge target becomes more honest after every volunteer must write the donation total they would plan staffing around.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: It took one silent pass of the pledge sheet for the room’s confidence to shrink.

exampleSpecs.domain: independent bookstore preorder estimate for a visiting novelist
exampleSpecs.stakes: ordering too many signed copies traps cash in unsold stock
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: You ask Mathieu to compare his confident preorder claim with the number he would have ordered if his own margin had been on the line.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: You are standing behind the register with three cartons of unsigned books at your feet.

skillTargets: detect when wager language becomes status pressure

tryThisNowSpec: Pick one claim you made strongly this week and write the confidence level you would stand behind if a colleague recorded it before the result arrived.
